title: De Ortu Et Obitu Patrum Qui In Scriptura Laudibus Efferuntur
author: Isidorus Hispalensis

passages.original: Vixit autem centum septuaginta quinque annos, sepultusque est in agro Ephron, in spelanca duplici in cujus interiori parte sepultum ferunt Adam, ia exteriori vero Abraham. Distat autem hic locus, ut Josephus edocet, septimo ab urbe Hebron stadio , ibique asserit Abrabam et filios ejus sepulcrum habere pulcherrimo instructum marmore.
passages.english: He lived one hundred and seventy-five years, and was buried in the field of Ephron, in the double cave, in whose inner part they say Adam was buried, and in the outer part Abraham. This place lies, as Josephus informs us, at the seventh stadium from the city of Hebron, and he states that Abraham and his sons have a tomb there furnished with the most beautiful marble.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'spelanca' read as spelunca, 'ia' as in, 'Abrabam' as Abraham.

passages.original: 16. Illic etiam, et terebinthum magnam arborem a constitutione 157 mundi fuisse asseverat. Hanc beatus Hieronymus usque ad Constantini imperium perdurasse scribit, ipsa est enim quercus Mambrae Amor. rhaei, qui fuit amicus Abrahae, quæ apud gentiles in tanta exstitit veneratione, ut eam muri ambitu circumseptam solemni veneratione colerent.
passages.english: 16. There also, he affirms, a terebinth, a great tree, had stood since the founding of the world. The blessed Jerome writes that it lasted until the reign of Constantine, for it is the oak of Mamre the Amorite, who was a friend of Abraham. Among the gentiles it was held in such veneration that they enclosed it within the circuit of a wall and honoured it with solemn veneration.
passages.notes: '157' is a page number from the printed edition and is omitted. 'Amor. rhaei' read as Amorrhaei (the Amorite).
